cohort: 350 antenatal women with singleton pregnancy in the first trimester, divided into two groups based on BMI (less than 25 kg/m2 and greater than or equal to 25 kg/m2).
finding: Women with BMI greater than or equal to 25 kg/m2 had a statistically significant increased risk of gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, IUGR, induction of labor, NPOL, and cesarean section compared to women with BMI less than 25 kg/m2.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were higher in women with BMI greater than or equal to 25 kg/m2 (48.57%) compared to women with BMI less than 25 kg/m2 (24%).
